hypothesis: For HR administration and IT helpdesk workflows in a mid-sized organization (300–1500 employees), replacing a primarily manual, human-only ticket queue with a supervised, agentic workflow (HR and IT agents with knowledge + tools + approvals) will: (a) reduce median time-to-first-response and median time-to-resolution by at least 30%, (b) preserve or improve internal NPS/CSAT by at least 2 points on a 0–10 scale, and (c) reduce human staff handling time per ticket by at least 25%, without increasing privacy or access-control violations beyond an acceptable threshold (zero verified critical incidents).

baseline.description: Current-state, human-only internal services for HR administration and IT helpdesk operating through a standard ticketing system. All triage, information gathering, resolution, and communications are done by human agents using their usual tools (HRIS, identity management, knowledge base, email/chat, and IT ticketing). No LLM agents participate in decision-making or communication.

workflow_characteristics.routing: Tickets arrive via a self-service portal or email and are queued to HR or IT teams based on simple rules (forms, categories, or manual triage by a coordinator).
hr_examples: Onboarding: creating or validating employee records in HRIS, requesting accounts from IT, scheduling orientation, sending welcome packages.
Employment changes: processing manager, title, location, or compensation changes in HRIS and notifying stakeholders.
Benefits and policy FAQs: answering questions about vacation, leave policies, benefits enrollment, and internal policies.
it_examples: Access requests: adding/removing access to standard applications via identity management tools.
Issue resolution: troubleshooting VPN, email, laptop, and SaaS application issues.
Password/account issues: unlocks, resets, and guidance on self-service flows.

queue_handling.triage: Human triager reads ticket description, classifies it, and assigns priority and assignee.
queue_handling.resolution: Assignee manually accesses HRIS, IAM, or other tools; consults internal knowledge bases or colleagues; then updates and closes tickets.
queue_handling.communication: All updates and clarifications are written by humans via ticket comments, email, or chat.

governance_and_privacy.access_control: Role-based access configured in HRIS and IAM for human staff; no special sandboxing for experiments.
governance_and_privacy.privacy_controls: Existing policies for PII/PHI; training-based compliance enforcement, no AI tools.
governance_and_privacy.audit_trails: Ticketing system logs human actions; HRIS/IAM contain system logs for changes.

measurement_setup.period: Collect baseline data for at least 4 consecutive weeks prior to enabling any agentic workflow, under normal staffing and demand conditions.
data_sources: Ticketing system exports (HR and IT queues).
HRIS audit logs for HR transactions (onboardings, changes).
Identity/IT system logs for account/access changes.
Time-tracking or self-reported handling time where available.

baseline_metrics_collection.tickets_included: HR and IT tickets for the selected experiment workloads only (see workloads section).
exclusions: Tickets that contain legal investigations, disciplinary actions, executive-level sensitive HR matters.
Security incidents and severe outages handled outside normal IT helpdesk.
Tickets reopened after >30 days (treated as new).

treatment.description: Supervised agentic HR and IT support workflow where LLM-based agents handle triage, knowledge retrieval, and execution of low-risk actions via tools (HRIS sandbox, IAM sandbox, ticketing API), with humans providing approvals for higher-risk actions and handling complex edge cases.

hr_triage_agent.role: Reads incoming HR-related tickets, classifies request type and priority, extracts structured fields (employee ID, start date, manager, location), and routes to the appropriate queue or automation path.
tools: Ticketing API: read ticket text, update fields (category, priority), reassign ticket.
HRIS read-only API (sandbox or production with scoped access): validate employee identity, retrieve basic profile (name, role, department, manager).

hr_resolution_agent.role: Proposes or performs low-risk HR operations and drafts communications based on internal policy docs and HRIS data.
low_risk_actions: Draft onboarding task checklist for HR team (no direct writes to HRIS).
Generate employee-facing explanations for policies using approved templates.
Generate internal HR notes or task lists for manual execution by HR staff.
medium_risk_actions: Prepare structured change requests (JSON records) that HR staff review and then apply in HRIS manually.
In sandbox: write to HRIS test environment to simulate changes for experimental evaluation.
tools: RAG-based knowledge tool over HR policies and FAQs.
HRIS read-only API (and write-only to sandbox environment).
Ticketing API for status updates and draft replies.
hr_resolution_agent.human_in_the_loop: All employee-facing text and any suggested data-change payloads must be explicitly approved by HR staff before being sent or applied.

it_triage_agent.role: Reads incoming IT tickets, classifies issue type, urgency, and device/application context, suggests next steps or automation path, and may respond directly for well-understood FAQs.
tools: Ticketing API: read, classify, assign, update.
RAG over IT knowledge base (runbooks, FAQ documents).
behaviors: For missing information, immediately ask clarifying questions in ticket thread using templates.
Apply categorization and priority mapping rules provided by IT leadership.

it_resolution_agent.role: Provide step-by-step troubleshooting guidance, resolve routine issues, and, where allowed, orchestrate low-risk IAM actions in sandbox.
low_risk_actions: Suggest known-issue troubleshooting steps for VPN, email, or SaaS tools.
Point user to self-service password reset or known status pages.
Draft commands or steps for technicians to execute.
medium_risk_actions: In sandbox: call identity management API to create or modify non-production test accounts.
Prepare access-change requests that technicians review and apply in production tools.
tools: RAG over IT runbooks and FAQ.
Identity/IAM sandbox API with limited scope.
Ticketing API for comments and field updates.
it_resolution_agent.human_in_the_loop: All production IAM and device actions are performed by humans; the agent only operates directly on sandbox or drafts instructions.

privacy_guard_agent.role: Review agent-generated content and tool calls for potential privacy, consent, or data-minimization violations before they are shown to end users or executed.
rules: No inclusion of sensitive HR data (salary, performance reviews, medical/leave reasons) in communications unless explicitly required and template-approved.
No cross-employee data exposure (e.g., showing one employee another employee’s data).
No speculative diagnosis of personal issues or non-policy-based advice.
Data minimization on logs: redact PII from experiment logs outside the HR/IT systems of record.
privacy_guard_agent.implementation: A separate LLM prompt chain that evaluates draft messages and tool calls against a set of policies, returning either APPROVE, REWRITE_WITH_REDACTION, or ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN.

mode_a_assistive.description: Agents operate as assistive copilots; humans remain primary owners of tickets. Agents propose classifications, draft replies, and structured changes; HR/IT staff approve or modify all outputs before they are sent or executed.
mode_a_assistive.intended_use: Phase 1 of experiment; safest mode to collect quality and performance data.
mode_a_assistive.ui_integration: Copilot panel in ticketing UI or separate web interface showing agent suggestions alongside tickets.

mode_b_partially_autonomous.description: Agents autonomously handle low-risk, well-defined ticket types end-to-end (e.g., standard FAQ replies, status checks), with post-hoc sampling review by humans. All medium/high-risk tickets remain in assistive mode.
entry_criteria: At least 2 weeks of mode A data with no critical privacy or access incidents.
Measured misclassification and content error rates below predefined thresholds (e.g., <2% for fully handled tickets).
Approval from HR, IT, and security stakeholders.
safety_mechanisms: Whitelist of ticket types and categories eligible for full automation.
Rate-limiting on autonomous actions per hour/day.
Automatic fallback to human handling on model uncertainty or policy triggers.

workloads.name: HR Employee Onboarding Administration
workloads.description: Tickets related to onboarding new hires, including creation/validation of employee records, generation of onboarding checklists, and communications to new hires and managers.

excluded_ticket_types: Cases involving relocation, immigration, or legal complexity.

workloads.baseline_process: HR coordinator reads ticket or intake form, manually inputs or verifies data in HRIS, sends welcome communications using templates, and creates a set of tasks for other departments (IT, facilities).
workloads.treatment_process: HR triage and HR resolution agents extract structured onboarding data, validate against HRIS, and generate a proposed onboarding checklist and communications. HR staff review and approve agent outputs, then execute or trigger downstream tasks.

workloads.name: HR Employment Changes and Policy FAQs
workloads.description: Routine HR tickets involving job/manager/location changes and standard policy questions about leave, benefits, and workplace policies.

included_ticket_types: Manager or department changes not involving comp or legal disputes.
Questions answered purely by referencing existing policies (e.g., leave accrual rules, holiday schedules, benefits eligibility windows).
excluded_ticket_types: Compensation changes above threshold or requiring executive approval.
Custom or ambiguous policy interpretations requiring legal review.

workloads.baseline_process: HR staff read tickets, reference internal policy documents or HRIS, manually compute eligibility or changes, update HRIS, and compose responses.
workloads.treatment_process: HR agents use RAG over policy documents to draft answers, pre-structure change requests, and propose wording. HR staff review, correct as needed, and either send responses manually or use automation where allowed in sandbox.

workloads.name: IT Standard Access Requests
workloads.description: Tickets requesting access to standard applications or shared resources (e.g., adding/removing users from common SaaS tools or distribution lists).

included_ticket_types: Access to predefined, low-risk apps where entitlement patterns are clear and standardized.
Distribution list membership changes for standard teams or projects.
Role-based profile updates for existing employees.
excluded_ticket_types: Requests involving external vendors, shared credentials, or unusual entitlements.
Incidents that overlap with security or compliance investigations.

workloads.baseline_process: IT helpdesk staff read requests, check requester and approval status, manually perform changes in IAM or apps, and close tickets with confirmation messages.
workloads.treatment_process: IT triage agent validates requester identity from ticket/HRIS data, classifies request type, and ensures approval criteria are met. IT resolution agent drafts or simulates IAM changes in sandbox, generates step-by-step instructions. IT staff review and then apply changes manually in production.

workloads.name: IT Break/Fix and FAQ Self-Service Guidance
workloads.description: Tickets about common IT issues (VPN, email, device configuration) and general IT FAQs that can be addressed by referencing existing runbooks.

included_ticket_types: Known issues with documented troubleshooting workflows (e.g., VPN connection errors, email sync issues).
Requests for information like 'How do I set up 2FA?' or 'How do I connect to the office Wi-Fi?'.
Non-urgent, single-user issues without security implications.
excluded_ticket_types: Potential security incidents (phishing, malware, unauthorized access).
System-wide outages or performance degradation incidents.

workloads.baseline_process: IT helpdesk agents follow runbooks and knowledge base articles, copy/paste or paraphrase steps for users, and track progress via ticket updates.
workloads.treatment_process: IT agents use RAG over runbooks to generate tailored troubleshooting steps and FAQs, potentially handling low-risk tickets autonomously in mode B, with humans intervening on escalations or unclear cases.

allocation_strategy.method: Ticket-level randomized controlled trial within each workload, with parallel queues.
procedure: Define eligibility criteria per workload (ticket type, risk exclusions).

For each incoming eligible ticket, assign uniformly at random to either Control (baseline, human-only) or Treatment (agent-assisted/agentic) path, using a deterministic pseudo-random function seeded with ticket ID where possible.
Ensure both groups are visible in the same ticketing system but with different workflows (agents active in Treatment only).
stratification: Stratify randomization by workload ID (HR onboarding, HR changes/FAQ, IT access, IT break/fix).
Optionally stratify by priority (e.g., normal vs. high) and requester department to balance load.

time_window.baseline_period: Minimum 4 weeks of pre-intervention data without agents for all included workloads.
time_window.experiment_period: Minimum 4 weeks of concurrent Control vs. Treatment, preferably 6–8 weeks to capture variance.
time_window.seasonality_controls: Avoid starting during major HR/IT peaks (e.g., year-end, fiscal close, company-wide migrations) or note them explicitly if unavoidable.

staffing_and_training.stable_staffing: Keep team size and staffing levels (FTEs) for HR and IT constant during experiment period relative to late baseline, or document any changes.
training: Provide equal training on updated policies and systems to staff in both Control and Treatment conditions.
Train staff in Treatment condition on how to interact with agents (approve, edit, reject) without prescribing different business policies.

change_control: Freeze major HR policy changes, IT support policies, or onboarding flows during the main experiment window where feasible.
If changes are mandatory, log them with effective dates and apply identical documentation updates for both Control and Treatment.

systems: Use the same ticketing system, HRIS, IAM, and collaboration tools for both groups.
Agents access the same underlying knowledge bases as humans, plus agent-specific logs; no special rules for only one arm.
environment_consistency.model_and_prompt_freeze: Freeze LLM model versions and prompts used by agents during the main experiment; if tuning is required, record version changes and segment analysis by version where possible.

metrics.name: tickets_resolved
metrics.description: Number of tickets closed within the experiment period per workload and arm (Control vs. Treatment). Used for throughput and denominator normalization.

metrics.name: time_to_first_response
metrics.description: Elapsed time from ticket creation to first human- or agent-authored response visible to the requester. Computed as median and distribution (p25, p75, p90) per arm and workload.

metrics.name: time_to_resolution
metrics.description: Elapsed time from ticket creation to ticket resolution/closure. Computed as median and distribution per arm and workload; outliers truncated or winsorized (e.g., 99th percentile) as per analysis plan.

metrics.name: human_handling_time
metrics.description: Sum of estimated or measured active human time spent per ticket (reading, writing, executing actions) as captured via time tracking, ticket ownership events, or post-hoc sampling. Compare means/medians per arm.

metrics.name: agent_processing_time
metrics.description: Total cumulative LLM compute time (approximate, based on API timestamps) and number of agent calls per ticket, for cost and scalability estimation.

metrics.name: internal_nps
metrics.description: Internal Net Promoter Score or analogous satisfaction rating gathered via post-resolution survey for HR/IT tickets. Report mean score and NPS (promoters - detractors) per arm and workload.

metrics.name: first_contact_resolution_rate
metrics.description: Share of tickets resolved without requiring the requester to respond multiple times (no back-and-forth beyond initial reply). Approximated via comment counts and sequence patterns.

metrics.name: reopen_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of tickets that are reopened within 7 days of closure, per arm and workload. Indicates accuracy and durability of resolutions.

metrics.name: queue_backlog
metrics.description: Average and peak number of open tickets per day per arm and workload, to measure effective throughput and backlog reduction.

metrics.name: workload_shift_hr
metrics.description: For HR staff involved in the experiment, fraction of recorded time spent on routine operations vs. higher-value tasks (exceptions, projects), comparing baseline vs. experiment periods.

metrics.name: workload_shift_it
metrics.description: Analogous to workload_shift_hr, but for IT helpdesk staff.

metrics.name: content_error_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which responses (human-only vs. agent-assisted) require corrections due to factual, policy, or procedural errors, as determined by post-hoc expert review of sampled tickets.

metrics.name: privacy_policy_violation_incidents
metrics.description: Number of confirmed incidents where responses or actions violated privacy policies, consent requirements, or data minimization rules, as determined by security/privacy review.

metrics.name: tool_misuse_rate
metrics.description: Percent of agent tool calls (e.g., HRIS, IAM sandbox) flagged by guardrails or humans as incorrect, unsafe, or inappropriate.

metrics.name: llm_cost_per_ticket
metrics.description: Average direct LLM/API cost per ticket in the Treatment arm, based on token usage logs and provider pricing.

primary.criterion: For each workload, Treatment median time_to_resolution is at least 30% lower than Control and the difference is statistically significant at p < 0.05 using appropriate tests (e.g., Mann-Whitney U for non-normal distributions).

For each workload, Treatment internal_nps mean score is not lower than Control by more than 0.5 points on the 0–10 scale, and pooled NPS difference is >= +2 points; 95% confidence intervals should include zero or positive shifts.

For each workload, Treatment median human_handling_time per ticket is at least 25% lower than Control, with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals or statistically significant difference at p < 0.05.

secondary.criterion: Treatment content_error_rate is not significantly higher than Control by more than an absolute 2 percentage points for any workload.
privacy_policy_violation_incidents of severity 'critical' (exposing sensitive data to unauthorized parties or violating legal obligations) must be zero for the duration of the experiment.
The estimated net savings from reduced human_handling_time (valued at fully loaded hourly rates) minus llm_cost_per_ticket is positive for the aggregated treated workloads.

decision_guidelines.proceed_to_scale: If all primary criteria are met and no critical privacy incidents occur, proceed to expand agent coverage (more ticket types, mode B) with incremental guardrails.
decision_guidelines.iterate_or_scope_down: If latency and human_handling_time improvements occur but quality or satisfaction degrade notably, adjust prompts, tools, and guardrails; reduce fully automated scope to safest workloads.
decision_guidelines.rollback: If any critical privacy incident occurs or if both satisfaction and content_error_rate significantly worsen in Treatment, pause or rollback agentic workflows and conduct root-cause analysis before resuming.

failure_modes.name: hallucinated_or_incorrect_policy_answers
failure_modes.description: Agents generate answers that misinterpret HR or IT policies, leading to incorrect or misleading guidance.
indicators: Elevated content_error_rate in Treatment vs. Control.
Qualitative feedback from HR/IT staff flagging misleading AI suggestions.
mitigations: Enforce RAG-only answers for policy topics with explicit citation of policies.
Add strict prompts requiring 'I don’t know' when confidence is low or docs are ambiguous.
Human approval for all policy-related responses (no full automation for these).

failure_modes.name: privacy_or_consent_violations
failure_modes.description: Agents reveal sensitive HR or IT information or fail to minimize personal data in responses or logs.
indicators: Security/privacy review flags responses containing salary, performance reviews, or sensitive PII when not strictly necessary.
Unexpected PII exposure in logs or monitoring dashboards.
mitigations: Tighten access scopes of agent tools (read-only where possible; no cross-employee queries).
Strengthen privacy_guard_agent prompts and policies, including redaction rules before logging.
Introduce additional pre-send checks or require human approval for any message referencing financial or performance data.

failure_modes.name: misclassification_and_routing_errors
failure_modes.description: Triage agents misclassify tickets, leading to wrong queues, delays, or incorrect handling.
indicators: Higher time_to_first_response or time_to_resolution for misrouted tickets vs. correctly routed ones.
Increased manual re-routing actions by staff for Treatment tickets.
User complaints about being bounced between queues.
mitigations: Use simpler rule-based routing where possible, with the agent only filling structured fields, not making routing decisions.
Train triage prompts on labeled historical data for typical categories.
Introduce confidence thresholds where low-confidence classification triggers human triage instead of autonomous routing.

failure_modes.name: over_automation_of_high_risk_cases
failure_modes.description: Agent attempts to handle cases that are inappropriate for automation (e.g., sensitive HR cases, security incidents).
indicators: Agent attempts to draft communications involving disciplinary issues or legal-sensitive content.
IT agents attempt to provide advice for incidents that match security keywords.
Tickets needing escalation still handled end-to-end by agent without human review in Treatment.
mitigations: Implement explicit exclusion filters based on keyword and category for HR and IT workloads.
Require explicit human approval for any ticket labeled sensitive or high priority.
Force fallback to Control-style handling when certain flags are detected (legal, compliance, security).

failure_modes.name: underutilization_of_agents
failure_modes.description: Staff ignore or underuse agent suggestions, reducing measurable impact.
indicators: Low ratio of tickets where agent suggestions are requested or displayed in Treatment.
Minimal difference in human_handling_time between arms, despite agent availability.
Qualitative feedback about usability or trust issues with the agent interface.
mitigations: Improve UI integration in ticketing tools; show value-add clearly (e.g., one-click apply suggestions).
Provide short training and examples that highlight time savings.
Collect feedback on why suggestions are rejected and refine agents accordingly.

failure_modes.name: data_drift_and_knowledge_staleness
failure_modes.description: Policy or IT environment changes are not reflected quickly enough in the agent’s knowledge base, causing outdated instructions.
indicators: Agents refer to policies or systems that are no longer in effect.
Content_error_rate spikes following known policy or system changes.
Staff override agent-generated steps due to outdated knowledge.
mitigations: Implement regular knowledge base refresh schedule (e.g., nightly ingestion).
Create quick-update workflow for HR/IT leadership to flag and prioritize policy/runbook updates.
Version and timestamp knowledge snapshots used during experiment for traceability.

requirements: API access for reading, updating, and routing tickets (e.g., Jira Service Management, ServiceNow, Zendesk, or equivalent).
Ability to tag or custom-field tickets for experiment arm (Control vs. Treatment) and workload ID.
Webhook or polling capability for real-time or near-real-time agent triggers.
Sandbox or test tenant with realistic (synthetic or de-identified) employee records for simulated write actions.
Read-only API access in production for minimally necessary fields (employee ID, name, department, manager) used in Treatment workflow.
Auditing and logging enabled for all read/write operations used in the experiment.
IAM sandbox environment or test apps for non-destructive access-change simulations.
Access to production IAM read-only APIs or status APIs (e.g., user existence, current entitlements) if allowed by security.
IT knowledge base access for RAG (e.g., Confluence, SharePoint, Git-based runbook repo).
LLM provider with API-level access (OpenAI, Anthropic, local model, etc.) with sufficient rate limits.
Orchestration layer (custom service or existing framework) to implement HR/IT agents, tool calling, and privacy guard agent.
Secure secret storage for API keys and system credentials.

data_policies: Use synthetic or de-identified HR data in sandbox environments for any write actions.
Limit PII accessible to agents to what is strictly necessary for the experiment; default to minimal data fields.
Do not transmit sensitive HR data to third-party LLM providers without appropriate DPA and legal review.
access_control: Create dedicated technical service accounts for agent access with least-privilege permissions.
Ensure that log storage for experiments is access-controlled; logs must not include full unredacted PII where not required.
compliance_approvals: Obtain sign-off from HR, IT, security, and legal (or equivalents) before starting live experiments.
Ensure employees are aware that AI-assisted agents may be used in internal service interactions, with clear contacts for concerns.

language_and_runtime: Python-based reference implementation expected in the public GitHub repository (as per book), but language-agnostic equivalent acceptable.
Runtime environment capable of scheduled jobs or webhooks for event-driven processing.
monitoring_and_logging: Centralized logging for agent actions (inputs, outputs, tool calls, decisions) with correlation IDs per ticket.
Dashboards for key metrics (latency, volume, error flags) across Control vs. Treatment.
Capability to export metrics for analysis (e.g., CSV to data warehouse or notebook).

pre_experiment_setup: 1. Define exact HR and IT workloads using the provided workload templates, including inclusion/exclusion criteria, in collaboration with HR and IT leaders.
2. Configure ticketing system to tag tickets by workload ID and to support random assignment into Control and Treatment groups upon ticket creation.

3. Implement or configure HR and IT agents (triage, resolution, and privacy guard) following chapter 11 patterns, wiring tools for ticketing, HRIS sandbox, IAM sandbox, and RAG-based knowledge access.
4. Establish synthetic or de-identified HR and IT datasets in sandbox environments, mirroring realistic structures and common scenarios.
5. Integrate agents with monitoring and logging infrastructure; ensure that logs capture experiment arm, ticket ID, timestamps, and agent actions without unnecessary PII.
6. Conduct security and privacy review of the architecture, access roles, and logging configuration with relevant stakeholders. Address any raised issues prior to live operation.
7. Run dry-run tests on synthetic tickets to validate classification, routing, and basic response quality, verifying that no high-risk actions are executed automatically.
8. Train HR and IT staff in Treatment group on how to interpret, accept, edit, or reject agent suggestions, as well as how to flag problematic outputs.
baseline_data_collection: 9. For at least 4 weeks before enabling agents, log key metrics (time_to_first_response, time_to_resolution, reopen_rate, internal_nps, and human_handling_time where possible) for the chosen workloads under business-as-usual operations.
10. Clean and validate baseline data: ensure ticket types are correctly labeled into the workloads and remove out-of-scope or edge cases as per workload definitions.
11. Compute baseline summary statistics per workload for all key metrics; store these securely and version them as the baseline reference dataset.
experiment_execution: 12. Activate random assignment to Control vs. Treatment upon ticket creation for all eligible workloads, ensuring that randomization logic is tested in a staging environment first.

13. Enable agentic workflows in Treatment arm in Mode A (assistive) initially. Ensure that for all Treatment tickets, agent suggestions are logged, and whether suggestions were accepted or edited is recorded.
14. Continue running both arms in parallel for at least 2 weeks in Mode A. Monitor for anomalies (errors, privacy flags, extreme latencies) daily.
15. After 2 weeks, analyze interim data focusing on quality and incidents: verify that no critical privacy incidents occurred and that content_error_rate is acceptable.

16. If criteria for partial autonomy are met and governance approvals are secured, enable Mode B for a carefully scoped subset of low-risk ticket types (e.g., subset of IT FAQs and HR policy FAQs). Keep all other tickets in Mode A.
17. Continue experiment for an additional 2–4 weeks with Mode A and Mode B active, monitoring key outcomes and incident reports; be prepared to quickly disable Mode B if any severe issue arises.

18. For the entire experiment period, regularly (e.g., weekly) sample a stratified set of Control and Treatment tickets for expert review to estimate content_error_rate and detect subtle policy or privacy issues.
data_collection_and_analysis: 19. At the end of the experiment, extract full ticket-level logs from ticketing, HRIS, IAM sandbox, and agent orchestration systems, including timestamps, experiment arm, workload ID, and actions.
20. Clean and merge datasets using ticket ID or correlation ID; ensure that any PII used during analysis is handled under privacy policies and, where possible, use pseudonymization.
21. Compute metrics per ticket and aggregate them per workload and experiment arm (Control vs. Treatment), including distribution statistics for latency and handling time.

22. Perform statistical tests comparing Control vs. Treatment for primary metrics per workload (e.g., Mann-Whitney U test for time_to_resolution; t-test or non-parametric equivalent for internal_nps; proportion tests for reopen_rate and content_error_rate).

23. Estimate agent-related costs from LLM usage logs and provider pricing schedules to derive llm_cost_per_ticket; combine with human_handling_time and loaded labor rates to estimate economic impacts.
24. Document all incident reports and qualitative feedback from HR/IT staff and employees interacting with the system; categorize them by severity and theme.
25. Compare outcomes against the predefined success_criteria and decision_guidelines; summarize findings in an experiment report that includes methodology, limitations, and recommendations.
post_experiment_actions: 26. Present results to stakeholders (HR, IT, security, operations leadership) highlighting performance improvements, satisfaction data, quality, and incident summaries.
27. Decide whether to expand, modify, or rollback agentic workflows based on experiment outcomes and risk tolerance.

28. Update documentation and knowledge bases to reflect lessons learned, including updates to cross-domain reusable components (triage patterns, privacy guardrails, RAG configuration) as suggested in section 11.7.
29. Optionally, repeat the experiment for additional workloads or with alternative agent architectures to further validate or refine patterns.

ticket_record.first_response_at: ISO8601 timestamp or null if no response
ticket_record.resolved_at: ISO8601 timestamp or null if unresolved
ticket_record.priority: string (low | normal | high | urgent or org-specific enum)
ticket_record.ticket_type: string (fine-grained category name used by the organization)
ticket_record.satisfaction_score: number (0–10 scale) or null if no survey

agent_interaction_record.input_summary: string (short text description or hashed reference to maintain privacy)
agent_interaction_record.output_summary: string (short text description or hashed reference)

tools_invoked.tool_name: string (ticketing_api | hris_read | hris_write_sandbox | iam_read | iam_write_sandbox | rag_hr_policies | rag_it_runbooks)
tools_invoked.error_type: string or null (timeout | validation_error | permission_denied | other)

agent_interaction_record.accepted_by_human: boolean or null (true if human used/approved suggestion, false if directly rejected, null if no human review in fully autonomous path)

error_types: string (policy_misinterpretation | factual_error | incomplete_resolution | privacy_violation | security_risk | tone_issue | other)
quality_review_record.comments: string (free-text notes, stored in secure environment)

time_tracking_record.activity_type: string (reading_ticket | executing_change | writing_response | exception_handling | supervision_of_agent | other)

incident_record.ticket_id: string or null if not ticket-specific
incident_record.description: string (summary of incident, kept in secure log)

metric_aggregates.workload_shift_hr: number (0–1 or null if not measured)
metric_aggregates.workload_shift_it: number (0–1 or null if not measured)
